learning: If max_error falls below about 0.058 m with line loss at zero, the excursion is a transient that derivative action damps. If it stays at about 0.061 m, the excursion is a fixed effect that neither gains nor geometry has removed in any race so far.
notes: Geometry is the iteration-2 row, held unchanged as the Builder proposed. The controller is the iteration-2 controller with kd raised from 0.05 to 0.15, the only change, to test whether damping reduces the 0.061 m start-up excursion. Report max_error and line_loss_events per track, and whether the excursion occurs at the start of the run.
rationale: The best-scoring row (iteration 2, 26.9949) has zero line loss on oval and slalom, and max_error sits at about 0.061 m. That is just past the 0.06 m off-track limit. Across iterations 0 to 8, max_error has stayed at 0.0605 to 0.0617 under every change tried: span, footprint, kp from 2.6 to 4.4, ki 0.3 (confounded), y from 0.02 to 0.06, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.10 and 0.15, and wheel_radius 0.04. Changes to kp and the sensor row therefore have not moved the excursion. The remaining untested controller lever is kd, the damping on signal rate. A start-up or entry transient that overshoots the 0.06 m limit would be the kind of disturbance more derivative damping can reduce. I therefore keep the iteration-2 geometry and controller exactly, and change only kd from 0.05 to 0.15. This is a modest increase, so steering noise should not grow much. Steering oscillation was about 0.07 in every race, so there is margin. The other controller values stay at the iteration-2 settings. Expected result: line loss stays at zero. max_error moves only if the excursion is a transient that derivative action damps. This is a prediction, not a measurement.
